title: Network-connected instrument
summary: A bench, table or inline instrument that is connected by a network cable or Wi-Fi rather than USB.
experience_text: No recording of a network instrument has reached us yet. This list is our best reasoning: the same start states, readings and endings as for USB instruments, plus what is special about a network (finding the instrument, a connection that drops, a new address after a restart). If the program's connection is encrypted, the tool can still keep sizes and timing, and says so. If your program offers something this list misses, please tell us.
before_you_start: The instrument, connected to your network the way you always use it, and the program you normally use, closed for now.
A sample or chart the instrument can measure.
If you know the instrument's network address (the program or the instrument's display may show it), have it ready. If not, the tool helps you find it.

The tool keeps only traffic to and from the instrument. Your other network traffic (web pages, mail) is left out before anything is written, but it is still a good idea to close programs you do not need.

blocks.label: connect
blocks.title: Start the program and connect
steps: Make sure the program is closed.
Start this block (the recording starts now).
Start the program and connect it to the instrument the way you always do.
Wait until the program shows the instrument as ready, then wait 15 seconds more.
blocks.note: Did the program find the instrument by itself, or did you type its address or pick it from a list?
blocks.why: How the program finds and greets the instrument is the first thing ChromIQ must repeat.

blocks.label: calibrate
blocks.title: Calibrate
blocks.only_if: If the instrument needs no calibration, record 30 seconds of the program waiting and say so.
steps: Start this block.
Start the calibration in the program as you normally do, and wait until it is done.
blocks.note: What did you have to do (a tile, a reference)? How long did it take?
blocks.why: Calibration is the first measurement-like conversation and usually the simplest to understand.

blocks.label: one-measurement
blocks.title: One single measurement
steps: Start this block.
Take the smallest measurement the program offers (one patch, one sample), three times on the same spot.
blocks.note: Did the program show numbers? Were they the same each time?
blocks.why: One short request and answer is the easiest place to learn the instrument's message format.

blocks.label: job-to-end
blocks.title: A small job to the end, saved
steps: Start this block.
Measure a small chart or a few samples to the end, the normal way.
Save the result in the program under a name you will recognise, and send that file together with the zip.
blocks.note: The name of the saved file.
blocks.why: A whole job paired with the program's own saved result lets us check every number.

blocks.label: cancel
blocks.title: Cancel during a measurement
steps: Start this block.
Start a job, and press Cancel or Stop in the program while it is measuring.
Wait until the program and the instrument are at rest.
blocks.why: A cancel is an ending ChromIQ must handle cleanly.

blocks.label: status
blocks.title: The instrument's information page
steps: Start this block.
Open the program's page that shows the instrument's details or status (model, firmware, lamp hours), look, and close it. Change nothing.
blocks.note: What did the page show (no serial numbers needed)?
blocks.why: Status requests show how the instrument describes itself, which ChromIQ needs to recognise a model.

blocks.label: modes
blocks.title: Every other mode
blocks.only_if: Only the modes your program offers.
steps: Start this block.
For each other measurement mode or condition the program offers, take one measurement.
Before each one, type the mode's name here and press Enter.
blocks.note: The modes you tried, in order.
blocks.why: Each mode may be its own command.

blocks.label: warning
blocks.title: A warning the program gives
steps: Start this block.
Create one harmless situation the program warns about, only if you are comfortable with it (for example start a measurement with no sample).
Read the message and answer it the normal way.
blocks.note: What exactly did the program say?
blocks.why: How the instrument reports a problem is what ChromIQ must understand and explain.

blocks.label: idle
blocks.title: Five quiet minutes
steps: Start this block.
With the program connected and idle, do nothing for five minutes.
blocks.note: Did anything happen on its own?
blocks.why: Network programs often send keep-alive messages; without them some instruments drop the connection.

blocks.label: cable-pull
blocks.title: The network drops for a moment
steps: Start this block (the recording keeps going).
With the program idle, pull the instrument's network cable (or, for Wi-Fi, switch its Wi-Fi off if it has a switch). Do not pull your computer's own cable.
Wait 20 seconds and read what the program says.
Connect it again and wait until the program shows it again (or says it cannot).
blocks.note: What did the program say, and did it reconnect by itself?
blocks.why: A dropped connection is an ending ChromIQ must survive.

blocks.label: power-cycle
blocks.title: Switch the instrument off and on
steps: Start this block.
With the program open and idle, switch the instrument off.
Wait 10 seconds, switch it on again, and wait until the program shows it again (connect again by hand if you must).
blocks.note: Did the program notice and reconnect by itself?
blocks.why: After a restart an instrument may get a new network address; the tool follows it, and we learn how the program finds it again.

blocks.label: close
blocks.title: Close the program
steps: Start this block.
Close the program the normal way, and wait 10 seconds.
blocks.why: What the program sends when it closes is what ChromIQ should do when it lets go of the instrument.

blocks.label: unexpected-end
blocks.title: The program ends by force while a measurement, then starts again
steps: Start this block.
Start a measurement in the program.
While it is busy, end the program by force (Windows: Task Manager (Ctrl+Shift+Esc), select the program, End task. Mac: Apple menu > Force Quit, select the program, Force Quit.) Type killed.
Wait 20 seconds. Start the program again and note what it does with the instrument (a new calibration, a message).
blocks.note: What did the instrument do when the program disappeared, and when it came back?
blocks.why: After an unexpected end the instrument is left as the program left it; how the maker's program recovers is what ChromIQ needs after its own unexpected end.

blocks.label: questions
blocks.title: A few questions
steps: No recording now. Answer the questions below; a short line each is fine.
questions: Which instrument is it exactly, and which firmware does it show?
Which program and which version did you use, on which system?
How is it connected: a cable to your network, a cable straight to the computer, or Wi-Fi?
Does the program offer anything that these blocks did not cover?
blocks.why: The recording cannot say which program made it or how the instrument is wired.
